I am 67 years old, and I have been working this land in Quzhou since I was 21. My bones know this soil better than any book. I have no schooling, but 46 years of watching the sky, feeling the wind, and learning from my mistakes have taught me what works here on the North China Plain.

This year, like last year, I will plant cotton on all 10.9 mu of my farm. Cotton is what I understand. It is what the buyers in Handan expect from us, and it is what my two-person household can manage. At my age, I cannot chase after many different crops. My husband and I can handle cotton together—planting, picking, and selling the seed cotton to the local trader.

I will till the field with rotary tillage in early April, when the soil warms. I buy improved cotton seeds from the supply shop in town. I know some old farmers still save their own seeds, but I learned years ago that the improved kinds resist bollworms better and give fuller boils. They cost more, but they pay back.

For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer as a base and add urea when the plants flower. In total, I figure about 18 jin of nitrogen, 7 jin of phosphorus, and 8 jin of potassium per mu. That is enough to feed the plants without wasting money on chemicals the soil does not need. The soil here is not rich, but it is honest soil.

Water comes from my well. Electricity for the pump is expensive, so I irrigate only when I must: four times this season—once after sowing if the spring is dry, once at flowering in July, once when the bolls are filling in August, and maybe one more if the autumn drought comes early. No more. Every yuan matters when there are only two of us.

I will spray pesticide five times. I do not spray blindly. I walk the fields every morning with my tea, and when I see aphids or bollworm moths, I mix the medicine and spray that same afternoon. Five times is usually enough if you watch carefully.

I expect about 100 kg of seed cotton per mu this year. If the rains come at the right time and the pests stay mild, maybe a little more. But 100 kg is a honest, safe hope for a woman my age. That gives me about 1,090 kg total. After costs, it will be enough for us to live another year and buy seeds for next spring.
